gotchas: Dialect is deliberately 'unknown'. Xantrex publishes that these products speak RV-C and, for the XC PRO, the CAN pinout — and nothing else. No DGN list, no scaling, no instance numbering, in any document on xantrex.com. The message definitions live in the RVIA RV-C specification, which is a third-party standard, not a

These models are grouped here by BUS, not by map, and that grouping is explicitly not a shared-map claim. RV-C assigns different DGNs per device class (inverter, charger, solar controller, DC source), so a battery monitor and an MPPT on this list certainly do NOT share a register map. The 30 PRO datasheet contradicts itself. The feature bullet says 'RV-C, Modbus and Bluetooth built-in'; the Communication row of the specification table on the same PDF says only 'Bluetooth, CAN Network (RV-C)' — no Modbus. The 60A datasheet is consistent about all three ('Built-in: CAN RV-C, RS-485 Modbus, and Bluetoo

The plain Solar MPPT 30 (710-3024-01) is a different unit from the 30 PRO (710-3044-01). Its datasheet and owner's guide list only a BTS port and a proprietary remote-panel port (710-0010) — no Modbus, no RV-C, no Bluetooth. Yet the Xantrex Gateway datasheet lists 710-3024-01 as a supported device. Contradiction record

'Freedom SW' spans two incompatible buses: the Xanbus 815-3012 (Modbus map exists, see xantrex-freedom-sw-modbus) and the RV-C 815-3012-02. The part-number suffix is the only thing telling them apart.
